items.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020
items.q: The guys that I’ve studied, they do. Like Coltrane for example, his thirst for knowledge was amazing you know.

ctx.x: It does make sense and it directs my next question, if it helps — you’re talking about aesthetics — do you think it helps an improvising musician to have a wide view of the world and have other interests like in other art forms?

The guys that I’ve studied, they do. Like Coltrane for example, his thirst for knowledge was amazing you know. So most of the — as far as I can tell the jazz musicians that I’ve come in contact with are extremely brilliant, they are really brilliant people. They are brilliant worldly people.
Yes. I wonder if you knew Kenny Davern?
